4800: from σύν and ζάω; to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively):--live with.
4801: from σύν and the base of ζεῦγος; to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage):--join together.
4802: from σύν and ζητέω; to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil:--dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together).
4803: from συζητέω; mutual questioning, i.e. discussion:--disputation(-ting), reasoning.
4804: from συζητέω; a disputant, i.e. sophist:--disputer.
4805: from συζεύγνυμι; co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian:--yokefellow.
4806: from σύν and ζωοποιέω; to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively):--quicken together with.
4807: of Hebrew origin (שִׁקְמָה) in imitation of συκομωραία; a sycamore-fig tree:--sycamine tree.
4809: from σῦκον and (the mulberry); the "sycamore"-fig tree:--sycamore tree. Compare συκάμινος.
4810: apparently a primary word; a fig:--fig.
4811: from a compound of σῦκον and a derivative of φαίνω; to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort):--accuse falsely, take by false accusation.
4812: from the base of συλάω and (the reduplicated form of) ἄγω; to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce:--spoil.
4813: from a derivative of (to strip; probably akin to αἱρέομαι; compare σκῦλον); to despoil:--rob.
4814: from σύν and λαλέω; to talk together, i.e. converse:--commune (confer, talk) with, speak among.
4815: from σύν and λαμβάνω; to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid:--catch, conceive, help, take.
4816: from σύν and λέγω in its original sense; to collect:--gather (together, up).
4817: from σύν and λογίζομαι; to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate:--reason with.
4818: from σύν and λυπέω; to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone:--be grieved.
4819: from σύν and the base of βάσις; to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place):--be(-fall), happen (unto).
4820: from σύν and βάλλω; to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack:--confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder.
4821: from σύν and βασιλεύω; to be co-regent (figuratively):--reign with.
4822: from σύν and (to force; causative (by reduplication) of the base of βάσις); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach:--compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove.
4823: from σύν and βουλεύω; to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine:--consult, (give, take) counsel (together).
4824: neuter of a presumed derivative of σύμβουλος; advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court:--consultation, counsel, council.
4825: from σύν and βουλή; a consultor, i.e. adviser:--counsellor.
4826: from the same as Σίμων; Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites:--Simeon, Simon.
4827: from a compound of σύν and μανθάνω; a co-learner (of Christianity):--fellow disciple.
4828: from σύν and μαρτυρέω; to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence:--testify unto, (also) bear witness (with).
4829: middle voice from σύν and μερίζω; to share jointly, i.e. participate in:--be partaker with.
4830: from σύν and μέτοχος; a co-participant:--partaker.
4831: from a presumed compound of σύν and μιμέομαι; a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary:--follower together.
4832: from σύν and μορφή; jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar:--conformed to, fashioned like unto.
4833: from σύμμορφος; to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate:--make conformable unto.
4834: from συμπαθής; to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate:--have compassion, be touched with a feeling of.
4835: from συμπάσχω; having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative:--having compassion one of another.
4836: from σύν and παραγίνομαι; to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid:--come together, stand with.
4837: from σύν and παρακαλέω; to console jointly:--comfort together.
4838: from σύν and παραλαμβάνω; to take along in company:--take with.
4839: from σύν and παραμένω; to remain in company, i.e. still live:--continue with.
4840: from σύν and πάρειμι; to be at hand together, i.e. now present:--be here present with.
4841: from σύν and πάσχω (including its alternate); to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"):--suffer with.
4842: from σύν and πέμπω; to despatch in company:--send with.
4843: from σύν and a compound of περί and λαμβάνω; to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one:--embrace.
4844: from σύν and πίνω; to partake a beverage in company:--drink with.
4845: from σύν and πληρόω; to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete):--(fully) come, fill up.
4846: from σύν and πνίγω; to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd:--choke, throng.
4847: from σύν and πολίτης; a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian):--fellow- citizen.
4848: from σύν and πορεύομαι; to journey together; by implication, to assemble:--go with, resort.
4849: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of συμπίνω; a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests:--company.
4850: from σύν and πρεσβύτερος; a co-presbyter:--presbyter, also an elder.
4851: from σύν and φέρω (including its alternate); to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage:--be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for).
4852: from σύν and φημί; to say jointly, i.e. assent to:--consent unto.
4853: from σύν and a derivative of φυλή; a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country:--countryman.
4854: from σύν and a derivative of φύω; grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to:--planted together.
4855: from σύν and φύω; passive, to grow jointly:--spring up with.
4856: from σύμφωνος; to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact):--agree (together, with).
4858: from σύμφωνος; unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note):--music.
4859: from σύν and φωνή; sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement):-- consent.
4860: from σύν and ψηφίζω; to compute jointly:--reckon.
4861: from σύν and ψυχή; co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment:--like-minded.
4862: a primary preposition denoting union; with or together (but much closer than μετά or παρά), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc.:--beside, with. In composition it has similar applications, including completeness.
4863: from σύν and ἄγω; to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably):--+ accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in.
4864: from (the reduplicated form of) συνάγω; an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church:--assembly, congregation, synagogue.
4865: from σύν and ἀγωνίζομαι; to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant):--strive together with.
4866: from σύν and ἀθλέω; to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly:--labour with, strive together for.
4867: from σύν and (to hoard); to convene:--call (gather) together.
4868: from σύν and αἴρω; to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account):--reckon, take.
4869: from σύν and αἰχμάλωτος; a co-captive:--fellowprisoner.
4870: from σύν and ἀκολουθέω; to accompany:--follow.
4871: from σύν and (to throng); to accumulate, i.e. convene:--assemble together.
4872: from σύν and ἀναβαίνω; to ascend in company with:--come up with.
4873: from σύν and ἀνακεῖμαι; to recline in company with (at a meal):--sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat).
4874: from σύν and a compound of ἀνά and μίγνυμι; to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with:--(have, keep) company (with).
4875: middle from σύν and ἀναπαύω; to recruit oneself in company with:--refresh with.
4876: from σύν and a derivative of ἀντί; to meet with; figuratively, to occur:--befall, meet.
4878: from σύν and ἀντιλαμβάνομαι; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist):--help.
4879: from σύν and ἀπάγω; to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield):--carry (lead) away with, condescend.
4880: from σύν and ἀποθνήσκω; to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to:--be dead (die) with.
4881: from σύν and ἀπόλλυμι; to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with:--perish with.
4882: from σύν and ἀποστέλλω; to despatch (on an errand) in company with:--send with.
4883: from σύν and a derivative of a compound of ἁρμός and λέγω (in its original sense of laying); to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly:--be fitly framed (joined) together.
4884: from σύν and ἁρπάζω; to snatch together, i.e. seize:--catch.
4885: from σύν and αὐξάνω; to increase (grow up) together:--grow together.
4886: from σύν and δεσμόν; a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control:--band, bond.
4887: from σύν and δέω; to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively):--be bound with.
4888: from σύν and δοξάζω; to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with:--glorify together.
4889: from σύν and δοῦλος; a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine):--fellowservant.
4890: from (the alternate of) συντρέχω; a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse:--run together.
4891: from σύν and ἐγείρω; to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to:--raise up together, rise with.
4892: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of σύν and the base of ἑδραῖος; a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal:--council.
4893: from a prolonged form of συνείδω; co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness:--conscience.
4894: from σύν and εἴδω; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of:--consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
4895: from σύν and εἰμί (including its various inflections); to be in company with, i.e. present at the time:--be with.
4896: from σύν and (to go); to assemble:--gather together.
4897: from σύν and εἰσέρχομαι; to enter in company with:--go in with, go with into.
4898: from σύν and the base of ἐκδημέω; a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller:--companion in travel, travel with.
4899: from a compound of σύν and ἐκλέγομαι; chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian):--elected together with.
